title: Genetics versus institutional training hypothesis

source.locator_policy: PDF page numbers 1-based; source paraphrased, no protected prose reproduced

context: As a child observer at the White Room, Arisu sees advanced trainees, including Kiyotaka, and discusses the institutional claim that exceptional achievement can be produced through training.
information_available: Only what Arisu can see through the restricted observation window and what the accompanying adults say; no access to hidden training data.
perceived_objective: Evaluate competing explanations for unusually strong performance.
observed_actions: Questions whether selection and inherited aptitude, rather than the White Room's training alone, explain exceptional student performance; proposes that successful trainees may have been genetically advantaged.
observed_result: Her father considers the hypothesis without treating it as proven; Atsuomi notices her analytical perspective. No causal explanation is experimentally resolved.
epistemic_limits: Arisu's claim is a child's source-bound hypothesis, not scientific proof about DNA, superiority or a general population ranking. Do not infer secret access to White Room data or automatic correct predictions.
memory_seed_policy: This is a pre-Y1 behavioral calibration case, not automatic actor knowledge of hidden school rules after divergence.
